sections.label: Our Teams

briefs.headline: Chelsea waits on Caicedo before today's trip to Arsenal
briefs.summary: Chelsea visits the Emirates at 11:30 a.m. ET with Moises Caicedo a serious doubt after his early exit from last weekend's Brighton win; Xabi Alonso said the squad call would come Saturday, and Jordan Henderson (wrist) also awaits clearance.

briefs.headline: Hannan's results from Roane and Logan remain unreported
briefs.summary: No outside source has posted a score for the Sept. 1 match at Roane County or the Sept. 3 home match with Logan; MaxPreps lists neither game and shows one win and one loss. The Wildcats host Point Pleasant JV at Ashton on Wednesday at 6 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Tottenham draws 0-0 at Forest for its first point
briefs.summary: Spurs drew 0-0 at Nottingham Forest on Saturday for their first point of the season and still have no Premier League goal; a Neco Williams header was ruled out by VAR for handball, and Roberto De Zerbi gave Destiny Udogie and Savio first league starts.

briefs.headline: Reds beat the Brewers 5-3 on McLain's seventh-inning homer
briefs.summary: Matt McLain's leadoff homer in the seventh broke a tie Saturday at Great American Ball Park; Elly De La Cruz and Tyler Stephenson also went deep, Tony Santillan got the win and Emilio Pagan his 21st save. The series finale is 12:10 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Crew blank the Rapids 3-0 to end a four-match losing streak
briefs.summary: Santiago Rodriguez headed in his first Crew goal in the 22nd minute Saturday and Gonzalo Tapia scored his first MLS goal in the 82nd, then set up Taha Habroune in stoppage time; Patrick Schulte kept the clean sheet at Lower.com Field.

briefs.headline: FC Cincinnati's match with D.C. United is postponed
briefs.summary: Saturday's match at TQL Stadium was called off over pitch conditions and player safety after inclement weather, the club said; no makeup date was set and tickets will be reissued. FCC visits Philadelphia on Wednesday at 7:30 p.m. ET on FS1.

briefs.headline: Penn State blanks Marshall 45-0 in Campbell's debut
briefs.summary: No. 18 Penn State scored 17 in the first quarter Saturday and held the Herd to 147 total yards; Carlos Del Rio-Wilson was 17 of 25 for 102 yards with an interception, and Rocco Becht threw four touchdown passes for the Nittany Lions.

briefs.headline: Ohio fades after halftime in a 49-21 loss at Nebraska
briefs.summary: Nick Poulos hit Riley Neer for 68 yards on the first play Saturday and the Bobcats trailed by one at halftime before Nebraska scored 35 after the break; Neer had six catches for 104 yards and a touchdown, and Jamal Rule ran for 122 yards and three scores.

briefs.headline: Pirates manage one run in a 6-1 loss to the Angels
briefs.summary: Yusei Kikuchi blanked Pittsburgh over six innings Saturday at PNC Park; Bryan Reynolds had three hits, including his 16th homer in the eighth, and Braxton Ashcraft struck out nine but took the loss. Paul Skenes starts the finale at 1:35 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: West Virginia holds off Coastal Carolina 31-24 in the opener
briefs.summary: Cam Cook had a 72-yard run and two touchdowns and Michael Hawkins Jr. threw a 49-yard score as WVU led by 24 at the half Saturday; Coastal got within seven with 27 seconds left and WVU recovered the onside kick. Pat White's No. 5 was retired pregame.

sections.label: Around the Leagues

briefs.headline: Rain washes out Aonishiki's Nagoya victory parade
briefs.summary: Ozeki (champion) Aonishiki's Tokyo parade for his Nagoya yusho (championship) was canceled Sunday because of heavy rain, Ajigawa stable said, and no makeup date is planned with the Aki basho (tournament) opening Sept. 13 at Ryogoku Kokugikan, seven days out.

briefs.headline: Guardians blanked 6-0, fall into a wild-card tie with Toronto
briefs.summary: Cleveland lost 6-0 to Detroit on Saturday as Toronto edged Kansas City, leaving the Guardians and Blue Jays level for the last AL wild card; Boston's Sonny Gray took his majors-leading 17th win in a second straight shutout of Baltimore.

briefs.headline: Michigan survives Western Michigan 13-12 on a Hail Mary
briefs.summary: No. 16 Michigan beat Western Michigan 13-12 in Ann Arbor on Bryce Underwood's 47-yard Hail Mary to JJ Buchanan after a review put one second back on the clock; the Big Ten said a Broncos defender had touched the previous pass while out of bounds.

briefs.headline: Pitt's Heintschel throws an ACC-record seven touchdowns
briefs.summary: Sophomore Mason Heintschel threw for 453 yards and seven touchdown passes to seven receivers as Pitt beat Miami (Ohio) 59-14 on Saturday, tying Pete Gonzalez's 1997 school mark; the old conference record of six was shared by 11 players.

sections.note: Sumo copy was read on Yahoo Japan article pages carrying Nikkan Sports' Sunday afternoon reports, with sumostats used only to find them; no Sunday update on Hoshoryu surfaced anywhere, so his status stands as printed Saturday, with the entry decision at the Sept. 11 bout-drawing meeting. r/Sumo was unreachable for a 14th morning; CBS scoreboards exceeded the fetch limit and MLB.com's scores page carried the finals.

coming_in.item: The general squirrel season opens Saturday, Sept. 12, and runs to Feb. 28: daily bag 6, possession 24, no season limit in the summary table.

coming_in.item: The youth bear weekend is Sept. 12-13, six days out; electronic registration is required and the limits are on pamphlet page 34, not in the summary table.

coming_in.item: The Marine Fisheries limits page effective Sept. 2 lists a 24-inch fork-length minimum and three per day; the Sept. 1 Fisherman's Post report has the Topsail shops saying kings are still thin and expected to move into 50-foot-plus water soon.

prime.item: Limits page effective Sept. 2: an 18-inch minimum and 27-inch maximum total length, one per day, and the division says possessing a red drum over 27 inches is unlawful; every kept red drum must be reported under the mandatory harvest reporting law.
Limits page effective Sept. 2: a 14 to 20 inch total-length slot with one fish over 26 inches allowed, three per day, and kept fish must be reported.

Limits page effective Sept. 2: a 14-inch minimum and 25-inch maximum total length, 10 per day; Coastal Angler's Sept. 1 Topsail column leads with black drum on cut shrimp at the bridges, docks and deepwater oyster rocks.
Limits page effective Sept. 2: no minimum size, and footnote M caps private recreational anglers at three per day, with five per day only in the for-hire fishery.

going_out.item: Day six of the two-week window, which closes at 11:59 p.m. Monday, Sept. 14: one fish per day, 15-inch minimum, hook-and-line and gig only, every kept fish reported when the trip ends. The division has published no harvest-to-date figure.
The youth squirrel weekend ends today, Sept. 6: daily bag 6, possession and season limit 12, details on pamphlet page 40.
going_out.publication: West Virginia Hunting and Trapping Regulations Summary, July 2026 - June 2027

going_out.item: The first gun window, in SELECTED COUNTIES only, closes Monday, Sept. 7; the county list is on pamphlet pages 33-39 and not in the summary table, so none is named here. Registration is required.

sections.note: Bird seasons, from the agencies' own publications: North Carolina's September teal season is Sept. 10-19 east of U.S. 17 only, six a day, with the first dove segment Sept. 5 to Oct. 10 at 15 a day, per the Wildlife Resources Commission's 2026-27 digest; West Virginia's first dove segment runs Sept. 1 to Oct. 11, 15 a day with a HIP card, per the DNR release carried by the West Virginia Daily News. Marine Fisheries' kingfishes (sea mullet) scoping period runs through Sept. 30, with the last public meeting 6 to 8 p.m. Sept. 17 at the Wilmington regional office. WVDNR's National Hunting and Fishing Day is Saturday, Sept. 19, 9 a.m. to 6 p.m. at Stonewall Resort State Park, adults $10 and 14 and younger free, per the agency's own page, which opened from here for the first time this morning; its elk management tours from Chief Logan Lodge begin Sept. 13 (wvdn.com), and the 56th Nature Wonder Weekend is Sept. 11-13 at North Bend State Park (Lootpress). Gauley season releases from Summersville Dam begin Sept. 11 with 22 release days through Oct. 18 (West Virginia Explorer); American Whitewater lists Gauley Fest for Sept. 17-20 in Summersville with 6 a.m. releases Sept. 18-20. Cobia limits are not printed: the division's page points to a proclamation this desk could not read.

waters.working: Up more than threefold from 53.7 cfs a day earlier, the biggest jump of the summer, after Saturday-morning thunderstorms drew a severe thunderstorm warning for Richwood, Camden-on-Gauley, Craigsville and the Cranberry area at the river's headwaters (NWS Charleston); the paper has no measured basin total. At 171 and carrying color this is a nymph-on-the-seam river, not a long-leader one: a heavy stonefly nymph or a weighted sculpin swung slow through the plunge pools and along the seams where the pocket water dumps in, with caddis, stoneflies and sculpin the forage. The front has passed and NWS Charleston's 2 a.m. discussion has dry weather through Wednesday, so the drop should be quick.
waters.note: The Forest Service's July 17 alert for the phased closure of Forest Road 86, the Williams River Road, from FR 216 to Route 150 is still posted with its Aug. 31 window and no completion notice; the agency says Tea Creek Campground and Three Forks are reached from Dyer. The Tea Creek bridge replacement that began Aug. 28 continues with the campground open.

waters.near: 14 miles above R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.read: 25.6 ft and rising - normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: Up from 25.04 feet a day ago and now about 0.7 feet above the National Weather Service forecast issued Saturday morning, which had the pool easing to 24.7 feet by Tuesday before the rain worked downstream. A little more push and a little more color on the pool, so the wing-dam tips and riprap still fish - shad are the forage, a white swimbait or a spoon over the tips at first light - with a football jig dragged into the slack behind the tips once the sun is up.

waters.near: below R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.read: 26.9 ft and rising - normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: Up almost a foot from 25.9 feet a day ago and above the Weather Service's Saturday-morning forecast, which had the gauge back to 26.2 feet by this morning and 25.7 by Tuesday. There is current on the lock wall and in the barge cuts again: a crawfish-colored jig pitched into the slack behind the cuts and a skipjack-pattern swimbait along the riprap where the flow pins bait against it.

waters.reading: Sound highs 4:07 AM at 3.4 ft and 4:51 PM at 4.5 ft at Hampstead; lows 10:37 AM at 0.2 ft and 11:43 PM at 0.7 ft.
waters.read: Fish the moving water either side of high at 4:07 AM and 4:51 PM in the sound.
waters.working: The Fisherman's Post September report, published Tuesday, Sept. 1 and five days old, has red drum steady at docks and creek mouths on early topwater, flounder "abundant" with quality 20-to-24-inch fish on a 1-ounce bucktail and Gulp trailer, bottom fishing off the Jolly Roger producing red drum, black drum, Virginia mullet, trout and the odd pompano, and black drum, pompano and croakers off the Surf City pier with Gotcha plugs taking Spanish; kings are still thin, and the shops expect them in 50-foot-plus water soon. Coastal Angler's Sept. 1 column adds black drum on cut shrimp at the bridges and oyster rocks. Flounder want moving water on structure, so work the flood into the 4:51 PM high; reds want the last of the fall, into tonight's 11:43 PM low. Waning crescent at 30%, so neap tides and a gentle inlet. Water 83.8F at Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast.
waters.note: Hampstead is the sound station and the read that matters; the oceanfront pier runs well ahead and is quoted only for a surf read. NWS Wilmington's 3:54 a.m. surf zone forecast has a low rip current risk on Pender beaches with 1-foot surf, patchy fog and a chance of showers and storms, and no advisories are in effect for the coast this morning.

kicker: Chelsea's trip to Arsenal kicks off at 11:30 a.m. ET; the Aki basho opens Sept. 13 in Tokyo, seven days out.
